construct: Inflammatory cytokines, especially IL-6, increase hepatic hepcidin production. Hepcidin binds ferroportin on enterocytes and macrophages, promoting ferroportin internalization and degradation. Iron export into plasma falls, producing low serum iron despite preserved or increased intracellular iron stores and ferritin.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Chronic inflammatory disease with normocytic anemia, low iron/TIBC, high ferritin, and high CRP reflects IL-6-driven hepcidin excess causing ferroportin loss and iron sequestration.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Increased release of stored iron from macrophages would raise circulating iron and is therefore directionally incompatible with the laboratory pattern.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Hepcidin-induced ferroportin internalization is the unique option that simultaneously explains low serum iron and preserved/increased intracellular iron stores.
